messages.author: 9cbdcb011f8600fa
messages.subject: CART output using party package
parts:
Hi everyone! 

I am conducting a meta-analysis, and trying to mine important influential variables on a continuous outcome variable using the party package in R.  
I have chosen about 8 predictors that I think might be important, and when I use the function ctree(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3.... x8, data = data), I get output showing my model, the number of observations (50), and line that says "1)* weights = 50". 
When I plot the model, all I get is a boxplot  (bar and whiskers plot) titled "Node 1 (n = 50). 

This is pretty uninformative, so I assume I am doing something wrong. 
Ultimately, I would like to determine which of these predictors (or interactions between predictors) are the most important, and move forward with ANOVA from there. 
Any suggestions for 1) what I might be doing wrong, and/or 2) books/readings that explain this simply? 

Thank you very much! 
Kristina

messages.author: 0c0915d54307a5d8
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: CART output using party package
parts:
I haven't used the party package for CART before, but it sounds like you are making a "tree" without any branches. I think you can use the "controls" argument to change the sensativity of your tree to make it more likely to branch. You may not have a significant relationship between your response variable and any of your predictor variables. The tree will stop branching as soon as it can no longer reject the null hypothesis. You can change your p-value with the "mincriterion" argument within the "controls" argument. (see ctree_control) in the documentation. You can also change the test type from "Bonferroni" to "MonteCarlo".

I have used rpart for CART analyses in the past, and found it pretty straightforward. It is more likely to give you a tree with way more branches than you know what to do with and you have to trim them down rather than trying to get them to branch more.

Hope that helps
Rosie

messages.author: 1f3baf5f4dbc25e1
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: CART output using party package
parts:
Hi, Kristina,

I recently used ctree and noticed that some of the predictors that were significant became insignificant when I repeated the analysis with a larger and more inclusive set of predictors.  The Bonferroni test type (one of the defaults of the ctree_control that Rosemary mentioned) "raises the bar" for significance for individual predictors when you add more predictors.  I ended up finding arguments to eliminate some of the predictors I fed to the model, and this gave me more partitions.  You can also relax the significance level, or change the test type (like Rosemary suggested).  

Julie

messages.author: 1bd043dc49f3e3c4
messages.subject: Re: CART output using party package
parts: Just to chime in here, I've used both rpart and ctree, and have encountered similar situations that both Rosemary and Julie mentioned. Definitely important to make sure you have no NA values in your dataset or it will likely throw out errors for MonteCarlo runs. Since the  party package uses permutation tests and statistically determines which variables are most important for use in creating splits, it is worth playing with the "maxdepth" variable, along with some of the other criteria (like relaxing significance values) when using ctree. In using rpart, I found it definitely seems to work more smoothly when you have categorical variables with many levels, but as Rosemary said, it does require significant trimming.  I found ctree easier to explain and understand once I figured out what settings seemed to make the most sense for the dataset involved.
